messages:
alicia: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — proposal to simplify the console query surface: centralize RBAC decisions at the gateway, mint short-lived capability tokens for fastpath queries, and fall back to full authz for heavy ops. Thoughts?

ben: Centralizing sounds good for latency but worried about coupling the gateway to policy churn. How do we avoid hot reloads/invalidations causing tail latency? :thinking:

chao: We can make tokens opaque and embed a small capability bitmap + expiry. Gateway check = local token decode + cache lookup; only on cache miss call authz-service. That avoids synchronous policy eval on the common path. Example token payload idea: 
```
{
  sub: svc-console,
  caps: ["read:dashboard","embed:tiles"],
  exp: 1719802800
}
```

dina: +1. For rollout: start by issuing tokens only for read-only dashboard queries from internal web clients, enable feature flag and canary 5% of traffic. We should also add a metrics tag to trace which path (token-fastpath vs authz-full) was used.

ben: Another perf note — token size matters if we send it on every request header. Consider short base64 token + gateway-local verifier keyed by KMS. Avoid sending big JSON. TTL should be small (30s-2m) to bound blast radius.

chao: Agree. Gateway verifier pseudocode: 
```
if decode_and_verify(token) and token.exp > now: allow_by_caps(request.path)
else: proxy_to_authz_service(request)
```
Keep capability checks fast (hash-set).

alicia: Security tradeoffs: minted capability token must be tied to client session and audience-locked (console UI vs api). We'll need rotation and an audit trail for token grants. Dina, can your team add a grant-audit event in the token issuer?

dina: Yep — will add a structured event: grant_id, subject, requester_ip, caps, ttl. Also add an eval_count metric for authz-service calls so we can detect regressions.

ben: Edge case: saved dashboards executed by background jobs (no user session). Suggest we fallback to a signed service token with broader capability but restricted to a queue worker identity. Log those separately.

chao: We should also plan for cache invalidation on role changes. Strategy: short token ttl + a revocation list lookup on sensitive ops. That keeps common reads cheap while still allowing quick invalidation when needed.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for console/gateway v2 with feature flag console.cap-token-fastpath = true (5% traffic).

alicia: Nice. Next steps: 1) chao/dina draft small RFC addendum describing token format + verifier API, 2) ben own perf load tests (latency + memory cost for headers), 3) ops run canary and collect fastpath ratio + authz-service QPS. Aim to gate wider rollout on <5% tail-latency increase and authz-service QPS reduction >=20%.

ben: I'll start a simple load script and add histograms for 50/95/99 latencies.

chao: I'll draft the code sketch + test vectors.

alicia: I'll create the follow-up RFC and link to this thread. If anyone sees a critical miss, flag here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary traffic at 5% stable after 10m. No errors injected.
